title: Finite-ring injective module sheaves are abelian-cohomology acyclic
statement: Let C be a category with a Grothendieck topology J, with abelian sheafification, Ext, and enough injectives for abelian sheaves in a common coefficient universe containing its morphisms. Let A be a finite commutative ring in that universe, and assume forgetting A-module structure sends sheaves to abelian sheaves. If I is an injective sheaf of A-modules, then for every natural n the underlying abelian sheaf has zero global cohomology in degree n+1. No finiteness is required of the sections of I.

source.place: subsingleton_H_forget₂_of_injective, lines 189-210; finite-ring coinduction proof of the comparison used in Stacks Tag 03FD.

proof.text: Embed the underlying abelian sheaf in an injective abelian sheaf B. Coinduction gives a monomorphism from I to Hom_Z(A,B), which splits by injectivity of I. Decompose the finite additive group of A into finitely many cyclic prime-power groups. The underlying coinduced sheaf is consequently a finite sum of retracts of the corresponding torsion kernels of B. These torsion kernels are acyclic by the injective torsion-kernel theorem. The identity of the underlying I factors as a finite sum through these acyclic sheaves, so applying positive cohomology gives zero. This argument is already a complete Lean proof in the attached source declaration.
